version.changelog: Remove child process login flow and add unit coverage

llm.summary: The skill's code, instructions, and required files are coherent with its stated purpose (automating Shanghai Library seat booking via saved auth or browser-assisted login); nothing obvious requests unrelated privileges or transmits data to third parties, but exercise caution before running the login automation and installing Playwright.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (library seat booking) align with the code and runtime behavior: CLI subcommands (availability, list, cancel, book) map to the documented library APIs and the code only calls the library's base host (yuyue.library.sh.cn). No unrelated cloud credentials, system-wide config paths, or external service tokens are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and the scripts limit actions to reading/writing local profile auth files, launching a local Playwright browser for interactive login (the user performs login manually), and calling the library APIs. The login flow extracts accessToken/sign/timestamp (expected for this integration). There are no instructions to scan unrelated system files or transmit data to unknown endpoints.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Registry entry has no install spec (instruction-only), but the package includes Node.js scripts and documents installing Playwright and its browsers. Installing Playwright will download browser binaries from upstream (normal but networked). No packaged download-from-personal-server steps were found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request environment variables or external credentials. It reads/writes profile JSON files under a user config directory (default ~/.config/shlibrary-seat-booking/profiles/*.json) to store accessToken/sign/timestamp and optional xEncode. This is proportionate to a client that must present the library's tokens.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true and does not modify other skills or global agent settings. It writes its own profile files under a user-scoped config directory (documented) which is appropriate for storing session tokens. The agent can invoke it autonomously (platform default) but that is normal for skills.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
What to check before installing and running: 
- Inspect login.js / login_and_get_auth_node.js yourself (they run Playwright and extract the library auth tokens). The extraction of accessToken/sign/timestamp is expected, but confirm the script does not send these tokens to any third-party servers. 
- The skill stores credentials in files under ~/.config/shlibrary-seat-booking/profiles/*.json. Keep those files private (chmod 600) and do not commit them to version control. 
- Playwright installation downloads browser binaries; run npm install and npx playwright install only on machines you control. 
- If you prefer manual control, you can manually capture accessToken/sign/timestamp from browser devtools and save them to a profile file; the scripts will use those tokens. 
- Because the skill's source is listed as unknown in the registry, prefer running the scripts locally after reviewing code rather than running them in an unfamiliar environment. 
- If you want higher assurance, ask the publisher for a canonical source (git repo) and a checksum, or request a security review of the login scripts; absence of such provenance lowers confidence.
